questions.questionText: According to Henry's Law, the concentration of a gas dissolved in seawater is:

options.text: Inversely proportional to its partial pressure above the sea
Proportional to its partial pressure above the sea, via an equilibrium constant
Independent of temperature and salinity
Only dependent on the gas's molecular weight

questions.questionText: Why is oxygen more soluble in seawater than nitrogen, despite oxygen having a higher molecular weight (32) than... wait, actually similar to argon (40)?

options.text: Oxygen is monoatomic, making it easier to dissolve
Oxygen is diatomic, so its electron cloud is more easily perturbed by water, increasing solubility
Oxygen reacts chemically with water molecules
Oxygen has a lower molecular weight than nitrogen

questions.questionText: What effect does increasing water temperature have on gas solubility?

options.text: Solubility increases because molecules move closer together
Solubility decreases because higher kinetic energy increases the probability of gas escaping the liquid phase
Solubility remains constant regardless of temperature
Solubility increases uniformly for all gases at the same rate

questions.questionText: What is the role of the ocean 'microlayer' in gas exchange between the atmosphere and the ocean?

options.text: It has no effect on gas exchange, since gases pass freely between phases
It is a thick layer where turbulent mixing dominates gas transfer
It is a thin laminar surface layer that controls the transfer of gases by molecular diffusion, and its thickness decreases at higher wind speeds
It only matters for chemically reactive gases like ammonium and sulphates

questions.questionText: In feature extraction, which level of image analysis focuses specifically on the outline of an object?

options.text: Boundary analysis
Region analysis
Whole image analysis
Texture analysis

questions.explanation: Boundary (shape/external) analysis focuses on the outline of the object, using methods like chain codes, Fourier descriptors, and signatures.

questions.questionText: Which method represents an object's boundary as a wave-like signal for shape description?

options.text: Euler number
Fourier Descriptors
PCA
Global Histogram statistics

questions.explanation: Fourier Descriptors represent the boundary as a wave, making them a boundary-level feature extraction method used for tasks like digit recognition and silhouette matching.

questions.questionText: Which feature extraction level would be most appropriate for distinguishing a rough fabric surface from a smooth one?

options.text: Boundary analysis
Region analysis
Whole image analysis
Chain code analysis

questions.explanation: Region (texture/internal) analysis focuses on the content inside the object boundary and includes texture analysis methods, used to distinguish smooth surfaces from rough ones like fabric.

questions.questionText: The Euler number, used in region-based feature extraction, specifically measures what property of an object?

options.text: The object's center of mass
The object's orientation angle
The number of holes in the object
The perimeter length of the object

questions.explanation: The Euler number is a region-based moment method that measures the number of holes in an object.

questions.questionText: PCA (Principal Component Analysis), used for whole image analysis such as Eigenfaces, differs from region and boundary methods primarily because it:

options.text: Requires segmentation of the object's boundary first
Only analyzes texture inside the object
Analyzes the image as a single entity without segmentation
Represents the boundary as a chain of directional moves

questions.explanation: Whole image analysis, including PCA for eigen-images, analyzes the image as a single entity without segmentation, unlike boundary or region methods which require identifying object outlines or interiors.
